newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Harvard plans to buy out fund shareholders.
newsitem.headline: Czech Harvard plans to buy out fund shareholders.

text.p: Czech fund manager Harvard Capital and Consulting (HC&C) said on Monday it has applied to the Finance Ministry to transform its closed-end unit trusts into open-end funds in order to "extend investment opportunities."

In a statement, vice-president Boris Vostry said once approved, HC&C would offer to buy out shareholders from the funds, which were created in the second wave of the government voucher privatisation programme, at a price equal to the net asset value per share.
"We have sufficient financial means available (to do so)," Vostry said.
Open-end fund managers are required by law to offer to buy out existing shareholders at full net asset per shares.
The statement said that current shareholders of any of the several HC&C managed "second-wave" funds would be able to sell their shares to Harvard as soon as the ministry approves the transformation.
But Harvard said that it would already start buying the shares from those who request to sell them, even before the ministry decision is ratified.
Harvard funds are trading at less than 50 percent of net asset value per share.
